373577.title: The arbor-polytope word-enumerator conjecture
373577.statement:
Let $\tau$ be an arbor of size $n$, let $\mathcal Q_\tau$ be its associated arbor polytope, and let $\mathcal D(v)$ denote the union of the blocks at the descendants of a vertex $v$, including $v$ itself. Let $\mathcal W_\tau$ be the set of words $w\in[n]^n$ such that, for every vertex $v$ of $\tau$, the elements of $\mathcal D(v)$ appear in $w$ at least $|\mathcal D(v)|$ times in total. Writing ${\rm des}(w)$ for the number of descents of $w$, **the arbor-polytope word-enumerator conjecture.**

$$
h^\ast(\mathcal Q_\tau,t)=\sum_{w\in\mathcal W_\tau}t^{n-1-{\rm des}(w)}.
$$

This is presented as a conjectural generalization of the preceding theorem and is supported in the source by extensive computer experimentation; no proof or resolution is supplied.

373609.title: The domatic game first-player difference conjecture
373609.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. Write $\operatorname{dom_g}(G,A)$ and $\operatorname{dom_g}(G,B)$ for the domatic game numbers when Alice and Bob, respectively, move first.

**First-player difference conjecture.** For all graphs $G$,

$$
\left|\operatorname{dom_g}(G,A)-\operatorname{dom_g}(G,B)\right|\leq 1.
$$

The conjecture proposes that changing which player moves first changes the domatic game number by at most one. The surrounding discussion notes that all known examples satisfy this bound, but does not establish it in general; the status is therefore open.

373673.title: The universal hyperbolic bound for block-structured coded retrieval
373673.statement:
Let $F_1$ and $F_2$ be files of sizes $s_1$ and $s_2$ with $s_1+s_2=k$, and let $G\in\mathbb{F}_q^{k\times n}$ be a rank-$k$ generator matrix. Write $E_i(G)$ for the expected retrieval time of file $F_i$.

**Universal hyperbolic bound.** For any partition $s_1+s_2=k$ with $\max\{s_1,s_2\}\geq 2$,

$$
\frac{s_1}{E_1(G)}+\frac{s_2}{E_2(G)}\leq 1.
$$

The bound is known for codes whose columns are entirely supported in one file, including local MDS codes, while the conjecture asserts it for all linear codes; the paper reports verification for all code families it studies.

373707.title: Matrix inequality conjecture for zero diagonal entries
373707.statement:
Let $M$ be a matrix with non-negative real entries, let $t$ be an odd positive integer, and let $(x_1,y_1),\ldots,(x_t,y_t)$ be distinct entries of $M$ satisfying $M_{x_i y_i}=0$ for every $i=1,\ldots,t$. **Matrix inequality conjecture.** Then

$$
\sum_{i=1}^{t}\sum_{j=1}^{t}M_{x_i y_j}M_{x_j y_i}\leqslant (t-1)\lVert M\rVert_{\infty}\lVert M\rVert_{1}.
$$

The paper formulates this inequality because it implies the weak balls conjecture and proves it in a special case; its general validity remains open.

373741.title: Connectivity of the reduced bumpless pipe dream graph
373741.statement:
For each $n$, consider the set of reduced bumpless pipe dreams of size $n$. A $2\times2$ flip is a local replacement of a valid $2\times2$ tile block by another valid tiling with the same boundary conditions. Only flips that preserve reducedness are allowed.

**Connectivity conjecture.** For every $n$, the set of reduced bumpless pipe dreams of size $n$ is connected under the $2\times2$ flips that preserve reducedness.

The unrestricted flips connect the full ASM lattice, but reducedness may obstruct this property and causes the standard monotone coupling approach to fail. Establishing connectivity would justify using these local moves on the reduced state space, although the paper does not resolve the conjecture.

373768.title: Karthick–Kumar–Sivaraman conjecture for fork-free graphs
373768.statement: Let $G$ be a graph. 373809.title: Schefler–Zhao–Zhong full-support conjecture for extremal separating atoms
373809.statement:
Let $G=C_{n_1}oplus\dots\oplus C_{n_r}$ be a finite abelian group with $1<n_1\mid\dots\mid n_r$. Let $A$ be a separating atom over a subset $G_0\subseteq G$ with $|G_0|\le r+1$, and suppose that $|A|=\beta_{\mathrm{sep}}(G)$.

**Schefler56Zhao56Zhong's conjecture.** The support of $A$ has full size:

$$
|\operatorname{supp}(A)|=|G_0|=r+1.
$$

The conjecture concerns the inverse problem for the separating Noether number of finite abelian groups: it predicts that every extremal separating atom uses all elements of the support permitted by Domokos' reduction. Exact formulas are known for several families, including groups of rank at most two and finite abelian $p$-groups, while a complete unconditional theory for arbitrary finite abelian groups remains open.

373840.title: Planar Circular Flow Conjecture
373840.statement:
Let $k$ be a positive integer, and let $G$ be a planar graph. A **circular $\frac{p}{q}$-flow** of $G$ is a flow $(D,f)$ such that every edge $e\in E(G)$ satisfies

$$
q\leqslant |f(e)|\leqslant p-q.
$$

**Planar Circular Flow Conjecture.** Every $4k$-edge-connected planar graph admits a circular $(2+\frac{1}{k})$-flow.

This conjecture is motivated by Jaeger's conjecture that every $4k$-edge-connected graph admits a circular $(2+\frac{1}{k})$-flow, which was disproved for all $k\geqslant 3$ by Han, Li, Wu, and Zhang. The cited counterexamples are nonplanar, so the planar case remains the relevant unresolved question.

373862.title: The common-zero independence-number conjecture
373862.statement: Let $G$ be a finite group, and let $\Gamma_v(G)$ be the graph whose vertices are the nonlinear irreducible characters of $G$, with two vertices adjacent when they have a common zero, meaning that there is some $g\in G$ at which both characters vanish. **Common-zero independence conjecture.** The following hold: (a) among any four nonlinear irreducible characters of $G$, two have a common zero; (b) if $G$ is solvable, then among any three nonlinear irreducible characters of $G$, two have a common zero. Equivalently, the independence number of $\Gamma_v(G)$ is at most $3$ for arbitrary finite groups and at most $2$ for solvable groups. This is presented as a weaker consequence of the three-class vanishing conjecture; the supplied text gives no resolution of it.

373912.title: Schützenberger's maximal-code commutative equivalence conjecture
373912.statement:
Let $C$ be a finite uniquely decodable code over the binary alphabet $\{a,b\}$. A code is **maximal** if, for every word $w\in\{a,b\}^{<\mathbb{N}}\setminus C$, the set $C\cup\{w\}$ is not a code. Two codes are commutatively equivalent if there is a bijection between them preserving the numbers of $a$'s and $b$'s in corresponding words. A code is prefix-free if no codeword is a proper prefix of another.

**Schützenberger's conjecture.** Every maximal code is commutatively equivalent to a prefix-free code.

The conjecture is presented as a restricted version of the disproved unrestricted conjecture. The supplied text does not provide a resolution of this maximal-code version; its status is therefore left open.

373928.title: The v-number bound for closed neighborhood ideals
373928.statement:
Let $G$ be a simple connected graph, let $S$ be the polynomial ring associated with $G$, and let $mathtt{v}(\mathcal{N}_G)$ denote the $\mathtt{v}$-number of its closed neighborhood ideal $\mathcal{N}_G$. Let $\mathtt{reg}(S/\mathcal{N}_G)$ denote the Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity of the quotient.

**The v-number bound.** For every simple connected graph $G$,

$$
\mathtt{v}(\mathcal{N}_G)\leq \mathtt{reg}(S/\mathcal{N}_G).
$$

The preceding theorem establishes this inequality for bipartite, very well-covered, and chordal graphs, and in particular for trees. The conjecture extends that phenomenon to all simple connected graphs; its general status is not resolved in the supplied text.

373963.title: Approximate Seymour second neighbourhood conjecture
373963.statement:
Let $G$ be an oriented graph, and let $N^+_1(G,v)$ and $N^+_2(G,v)$ denote the first and second out-neighbourhoods of $v$.

**Approximate Seymour conjecture.** For every $epsilon>0$, every oriented graph $G$ has at least one vertex $v$ satisfying

$$
|N^+_2(G,v)| \geq (1-\epsilon)|N^+_1(G,v)|.
$$

The paper states this as an equivalent reformulation of Seymour's second neighbourhood conjecture, obtained using lexicographic products; it remains open together with the original conjecture.

373965.title: Classification conjecture for Seymour Cayley orientations
373965.statement:
Let $G$ be a group and let a **Seymour Cayley orientation** mean a Cayley orientation in which every vertex has equally large first and second out-neighbourhoods.

**Cayley classification conjecture.** Every Seymour Cayley orientation can be constructed by taking, possibly repeatedly, lexicographic products of empty graphs, powers of directed cycles, and regular tournaments.

The paper proves this classification for Cayley orientations of abelian groups. The conjecture asks whether the same description holds for Seymour Cayley orientations over arbitrary groups.

373966.title: Distance-transitive Seymour-tight orientation conjecture
373966.statement:
A **Seymour-tight orientation** is an orientation $G$ in which every vertex $v$ satisfies $|N^+_2(G,v)|=|N^+_1(G,v)|$. A digraph is **distance-transitive** when its automorphism group is transitive on ordered pairs of vertices at each fixed directed distance.

**Distance-transitive Seymour-tightness conjecture.** Every distance-transitive digraph is a Seymour-tight orientation.

Directed cycles, Paley tournaments, and certain lexicographic products provide known distance-transitive Seymour-tight examples. The proposed conjecture seeks a complete structural property for all distance-transitive digraphs and remains open.

374128.title: Pardey and Rautenbach's bounded-deviation conjecture for colour-balanced matchings
374128.statement:
Let $K_{2kt}$ be the complete graph on $2kt$ vertices, and let $c\colon E(K_{2kt})\to [k]$ be a $k$-edge-colouring. Call $c$ **colour-balanced** if every colour appears equally often, and for a perfect matching $M$ define

$$
f_c(M)=\sum_{i=1}^k\left|\left|c^{-1}(i)\cap M\right|-t\right|.
$$

**Pardey and Rautenbach's conjecture.** For all integers $k\geq 2$ and $t\geq 1$, every colour-balanced $k$-edge-coloured $K_{2kt}$ admits a perfect matching $M$ satisfying $f_c(M)=O(k^2)$.

This asks for a uniformly controlled colour imbalance in a perfect matching, extending the known bound $f_c(M)\leq 2$ when $k=3$. The conjecture remains open in the supplied source.

374139.title: The dominant-zero-column singularity conjecture for random combinatorial matrices
374139.statement:
Let $M$ be a random combinatorial matrix, and let $\Omega_0$, $\Omega_r$, and $\Omega_c$ be respectively the events that $M$ has a zero column, contains two identical rows, and contains two identical columns.

**Singularity-obstruction conjecture.** If $c\in(0,1/2)$ is fixed and

$$
2\log n\leq d\leq cn,
$$

then

$$
\mathbb{P}(M\text{ is singular})=(1+o(1))\mathbb{P}(\Omega_0).
$$

The conjecture asserts that, in this sparse-to-intermediate regime, zero columns account asymptotically for all singularity. The supplied text gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
